# Hopf Frame Compilation

> Exact and Fault-Tolerant Compilation of Hopf Differential Frames, by Ruge Lin. Proofs and finite checks for prescribed complete Hopf frames under exact one-qubit/CNOT and coherent Clifford+T resource models.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation

## Use this repository for

- Exact full-frame size, CNOT-count, and clean-workspace/depth tradeoffs.
- T-count versus accuracy and clean/dirty workspace, including one-clean synthesis.
- Simultaneous one-clean real and phase-dressed complex magnitude-frame T-count/T-depth bounds at family-specific dirty reservations.
- Literal diagonals, complete one-target multiplexors, and fixed-decoder Hopf QBP robustness.
- Packed two-clean diagonals and precision-uniform one-clean O(N+L) real and complex magnitude frames, with optimal banked T-count and sharp high-precision endpoints.

## Selected claims

Start with manuscript/PUBLICATION_SCOPE.md for the complete hypotheses and formulas; docs/README.md maps every proof dependency.

- A: Exact real and phase-dressed complex magnitude frames have size Theta(N), CNOT count Theta(N) for n>=2 (zero for n=1), and depth Theta(n+N/(n+m)) for every clean budget m>=0, N=2^n.
- B: T*=Theta(sqrt(NL)+L+NL/q), G=O(NL), for real and complex magnitude frames with sufficient clean allocation a>=C(n+h), q=n+a+b, h=1+ceil(log2(L+n+2)).
- C: Optimal one-clean count for all n>=1 and integer L>=6. Fix a=1; the base dirty reservation is B=L+n+7 for complete real frames and B=L+n+8 for phase-dressed complex magnitude frames. At every b>=B, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). At every b>=2B, T*=Theta(sqrt(NL)+L+NL/b), with G=O(NL) for the upper construction. At EXACTLY b=B and L>=max(6,n), T*=Theta(N+L). Do not infer a matching transition at every B<b<2B or a new T-depth guarantee.
- D: One-clean all-precision theorem R72, research/depth/ONE_CLEAN_DEPTH.md. For all n>=1, integer L>=6, a=1, and b>=17(L+n+7) for real frames or b>=17(L+n+8) for prescribed phase-dressed complex magnitude frames D_phi W_real, one circuit has full error at most 2^(-L), T=O(sqrt(NL)+L+NL/b), G=O(NL), and D_T=O(NL/b^2+F), F=min{nL,(sqrt(n)+L)log2(n+L+2)}, with absolute constants. Count is optimal at every eligible width. Depth also matches through b<=sqrt(NL/F) when the interval is nonempty. For L>N/n^2 the stronger depth is O(NL/b^2+L). Native one-clean layer words, protected terminal flag relocation, a separate width/precision splice, and bounded dimensions are charged. A one-clean literal-diagonal schedule composes half-error factors on the same flag and dirty pool, retaining prior leakage and literal phases. R70 (ALL_PRECISION_DEPTH.md) and R71 (COMPLEX_FRAME_DEPTH.md) retain their two-clean statements and supporting proof roles. No arbitrary complex-unitary synthesis or unrestricted depth optimality follows.
- Retained two-clean real-frame linear-precision special case: for some absolute c>0 and 6<=L<=cn, research/depth/SUBLINEAR_T_DEPTH.md Section 10 retains F=min{nL,(sqrt(n)+L)log2(n+2)} and T=O(sqrt(NL)+NL/b) at the same dirty threshold. Early phase-gradient preparation and the terminal binary geometric source are separately charged; see SHARED_GRADIENT_RECOVERY.md and SHARED_BINARY_TERMINAL.md. At sufficient b=Theta(sqrt(NL)), L=o(n/log(n+2)) gives sublinear depth; fixed accuracy retains O_eta(sqrt(n)log(n+2)). GROUPED_TERMINAL_DEPTH.md retains its whole-word prefetch interface and standalone grouped alternative.
- Earlier two-clean results remain valid. At L=N the sharper endpoint keeps a=2 and b=N+n+7 for BOTH families and gives 2N-1<=T*<=O(N), hence T*=Theta(N). The one-clean real theorem attains the same count and dirty width; the one-clean complex theorem reserves N+n+8.
- Depth obstructions: docs/OPEN_PROBLEM.md is the authoritative frontier. For the complete-frame witness with cos(2theta)=1/3, R73 gives a positive three-layer error floor for each fixed clean budget; R74 makes that threshold explicit and requires minimum middle crossing rank Omega_a(sqrt(L)) for four-layer approximation at error 2^(-L). R75 requires at least five layers with zero clean qubits at integer L>=3, uniformly in dirty width; with one clean qubit, error below sin(pi/8)/(2sqrt(2)) forces exact terminal clean-sector preservation.
- Restricted one-clean frontier for the same witness: R76 gives the five-layer obstruction at L>=3 for a Pauli encoded midpoint, and a positive explicit floor for a Hermitian-Clifford midpoint. R77 gives a positive explicit floor depending on inner clean spread, even for non-Clifford midpoints, when either two-layer encoder has bounded spread. At error 2^(-L), every four-layer representation needs Omega(log log L) clean-active axes in each outer layer; R74 forces growing middle layers. These are necessary size conditions. The unrestricted one-clean four-layer question and optimal large-width depth remain open; terminal return alone does not supply the midpoint or bounded-spread hypotheses.

Here 0<eta<=1/64 and L=max{6,ceil(log2(1/eta))}. Upper bounds hold for all admitted parameters; matching lower bounds are worst-case over the named family. T-depth permits arbitrary Clifford interlayers and is not total depth. Supplied parameters admit certified evaluation; classical preprocessing is separate from quantum gate counts.

The full initialized-isometry contract includes arbitrary logical and dirty/reference inputs, literal phases, and clean leakage. Return promises depend on the construction: exact synthesis returns all work exactly; B returns dirty work exactly; one-clean operator-core return is approximate within the norm. Actual adjoints and inactive conditional-work sectors are essential. No QRAM, reset, postselection, supplied catalyst, or free evaluator is assumed.

## Read by purpose

- [Claim-led argument](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/REVIEW.md): The problem, A-D, their proof mechanisms, and operational consequence.
- [Selected claim ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/manuscript/PUBLICATION_SCOPE.md): Canonical assumptions, formulas, retained corollaries, and limits.
- [Proof dependencies](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/README.md): A-D, the sharper two-clean endpoint, and their supporting lemmas.
- [Verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/VERIFICATION.md): Evidence by claim, reproduction, and implementation boundaries.
- [Source map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/SOURCE_MAP.md): Imported premises and local contributions; stable detailed catalogue linked there.
- [Resource questions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPEN_PROBLEM.md): Precision-uniform one-clean real and complex magnitude count, optimal banked count, sharp high-precision endpoints, and the remaining large-workspace depth question for the stated frame families; literal targets and scoped reductions.
- [Research results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/research/README.md): The precision-uniform growing-source theorem and its dependencies, earlier restricted compilers, scoped representation limits, and preserved evidence. Consult this catalogue for individual research routes; their local open steps do not reopen the resolved count theorem.
- [Packed diagonal compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPERATOR_SOURCE_COMPILER.md): Section 8 gives error 2^(-ell), T=O(N+ell), G=O(N ell), two clean flags, and b=n+1+ceil((ell+4)/2); matching banked bound at twice that base reservation.
- [Result C: one-clean count](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/research/endpoint/GROWING_SOURCE_COMPILER.md#11-precision-uniform-one-clean-count): Canonical base and banked statements for all n>=1; Section 12 supplies the banked proof. Growing sources separate precision from logical mode allocation. A borrowed conjugate signal leaves the genuine initialized recovery anchor intact. Exact dirty queries preserve complete native masks and actual replay. The layerwise baseline covers L<=N/n^2 and bounded n; no iterated grouping premise is required. Literal phase dressing reuses the sole clean flag and dirty pool under the full initialized-isometry bound. Section 9 retains the sharper TWO-clean complex endpoint.
- [Result D: one-clean count and depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/research/depth/ONE_CLEAN_DEPTH.md): Both complete-frame families, all dimensions and precisions, native flag/workspace schedules, and full-isometry phase composition at the stated dirty reservations.
- [Finite-evidence catalogue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/reference/VERIFICATION_CATALOGUE.md): Proof-to-module/test correspondence, exact finite native words, bounded matrix diagnostics, and their separate evidence limits.
- [Completed state-based QBP supplement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/supplements/state_based_qbp/README.md): Different-decoder results with their own proof, cost, and native-evidence map; not a fine complete-frame compiler or an application speedup claim.

## Status and attribution

Result C's authoritative statement is GROWING_SOURCE_COMPILER Section 11, with the banked argument in Section 12. Its proof includes the n=1,2 baseline and precision lower bound. Section 10 retains the earlier two-clean argument, while Section 9 preserves the sharper two-clean complex endpoint. The historical source register keeps R64 and R65 as the original uniform and banked claims; their supporting primitives remain separately scoped. The current CORE_CLAIM_AUDIT reconstructs the selected proof chain, with dated audits retained as historical records. Optimal large-workspace T-depth remains open beyond the stated matching interval. Source- and query-specific obstructions remain distinct from unrestricted lower bounds. Internal review and finite tests are not external peer review, formal proof certification, or a general native emitter.

Use the exact consulted commit and CITATION.cff for attribution. The repository is MIT licensed. Collaborations: gogoko699@gmail.com.
